prompts.name: Crescent Harbor
prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: one new ASYMMETRIC SPATIAL-LAYOUT MOCKUP for Wayfarer, a civilian voxel spaceport with multiple functional relay islands.
REFERENCES: Image 1 is the ORIGINAL WAYFARER station model and supplies the recognizable central station architecture. Image 2 supplies the relay-island design language, power cables and active-spaceport materials ONLY. The four-corner symmetric layout in image 2 is explicitly REJECTED. Discard its composition completely and stage a substantially new spatial arrangement described below.

Keep one recognizable Wayfarer main station: open octagonal habitation ring, tall tiered port-control tower, radial bridges, warm cabin windows, two modest enclosed greenhouses, projecting launch apron and freight pier. Keep its original solar wings REMOVED. Supporting islands are substantial industrial platforms with stepped thick understructures, transformer/relay pylons, stacked capacitor cabinets, cooling grilles, ceramic insulators, copper busbars and heavy cable sockets. Clearly differentiate the islands by function, footprint, silhouette and size: charging, freight handling, repair cradles, fuel depot, traffic control, auxiliary power. Some compact tall masts, some wider low platforms. No identical square pads repeated around a hub.
Use thick bundles of 3–4 separate graphite armored power cables with copper clamps and reinforced connectors. Flexible shallow curves, solid endpoints, visibly connecting the architecture; inter-island connections are welcome. Cable routing supports the chosen spatial design and keeps ship approaches clear.
Show a calm working SPACEPORT: tiny varied couriers, passenger shuttles, freighters, cargo tugs, repair drones; ships arriving toward free berths, others docked, others departing with short restrained blue engine plumes. Around 10–14 varied small craft distributed among the main station and service islands. Keep ships much smaller than architecture, with no overcrowding, warships or combat.

VISUAL STYLE: faithfully preserve the rich cubic voxel 3D game-art look of the references: stepped block geometry, detailed but legible ivory alloy/navy/copper construction, crisp pixel-scale panels, warm amber windows, cyan guidance and power lights. Strong large forms with grouped mechanical detail and uncluttered flight-space gaps. Premium soft directional light and ambient occlusion against very dark blue sparse stars. All architecture fully in frame with comfortable margins. Wide landscape approximately 16:9, one coherent isometric/three-quarter scene, not a collage. No text, labels, arrows, schematic overlay, HUD, border, watermarks, giant planets or solar-panel wings.
NON-NEGOTIABLE LAYOUT QUALITY: dramatic asymmetry at first glance. No four corners surrounding a centered hub, no evenly spaced radial spokes, no evenly spaced orbit ring, no X or plus-sign layout, no bilateral mirroring, no equally sized and equally distant satellites. Novel but plausible organic port growth, deliberate unequal distances, varied heights, rotated footprints and meaningful negative space. The new arrangement must be the most obvious change from reference 2.

SPECIFIC DESIGN A — CRESCENT HARBOR:
Place the main Wayfarer station OFF-CENTER in the lower-left part of the image, its launch apron pointing into a broad empty harbor basin toward the lower-right. FIVE relay islands form an uneven loose CRESCENT trailing from behind the station across the upper half and down the far right edge. This crescent is open toward the foreground; never close it into a ring.
Build an intentional asymmetric sequence: a tiny tall auxiliary-power mast close behind the station at upper-left, a medium charging island higher and farther right, a LARGE low cargo dock as the far upper-right anchor, a small traffic-control island close to that cargo dock, and a separate medium repair/refueling platform farther down the right edge, rotated inward. A close unequal pair and one long gap create an irregular rhythm. Main station remains the dominant single structure.
Heavy power cables run along the BACK edge of the crescent, from the station to the nearby relay, onward between neighboring islands; one secondary branch serves the charging platform. Do not run cables through the open harbor basin. Two or three merchant ships traverse the broad empty basin toward the main apron and right-side berths; small tugs service cargo at the far edge. The scene should feel like a sheltered coastal harbor translated into orbital infrastructure. Preserve generous diagonal flight lanes and make the empty arrival basin a major visual feature.

SPECIFIC DESIGN B — BRANCHING RELAY CHAIN:
Place the main station toward the UPPER-LEFT end of a long diagonal spaceport network. It is the head of an irregular branching chain, NOT the center of a wheel. SIX relay/service islands extend diagonally away toward the lower-right, with changing distances, sizes, rotations and levels. The main station uses only ONE substantial trunk power connection from its lower-right side; the islands distribute power onward using inter-island cable bundles.
A medium power-distribution island immediately beyond Wayfarer is the first junction. Continue down/right to a large cargo-and-repair platform, then a smaller fuel relay, then a tall narrow terminal charging station near the far lower-right tip. Add two unequal side branches: one tiny sensor/traffic-control perch above the trunk near the first junction and one wider repair cradle below/left of the large cargo island. NO left-right paired branches, no zigzag decorative beads, no line of identical squares. Each branch has real service equipment and a berth.
Let the central trunk read as linked industrial neighborhoods, with ample gaps and cables visible between them. Ships move alongside the chain in an open arrival/departure corridor, with a freighter docking at the broad middle platform and couriers continuing toward Wayfarer. A few craft peel off to service islands. Keep the diagonal silhouette striking, stretching across the wide image with most empty space on opposing sides of the network. This should look like an organically extended orbital port with branching streets formed by cable infrastructure, visibly different from a surrounding-satellite composition.

Novel but plausible organic port growth, deliberate unequal distances, varied heights, rotated footprints and meaningful negative space. SPECIFIC DESIGN C — LAYERED SPACEPORT:
Use actual THREE-DIMENSIONAL HEIGHT AND DEPTH to make an unusual asymmetric multi-level harbor. Put the main Wayfarer station in the upper-right/rear of the scene at the highest broad inhabited level, seen from a slightly lower three-quarter angle so its underside and vertical separations are clear. Preserve the station shape and tower. FIVE satellites are staggered irregularly in height and depth, NOT merely placed around it in the same plane.
The largest satellite is a broad CARGO/REPAIR island in the lower-left foreground, substantially BELOW the main ring, with a freighter moored at a tall-sided berth. A tiny tall power-relay tower floats ABOVE and behind the main station toward upper-middle/left. A compact charging island hangs just below the main station's left rim, but with visible free space separating them. A medium fuel platform floats farther to the right and lower than Wayfarer, rotated obliquely. A small maintenance/drone perch sits farther back at middle-left, nearly edge-on and visibly more distant.
Use 3–4 dark armored power cables per connection, routed in sweeping descending curves and a few rising links, with reinforced junctions visible on different heights of the islands. A descending connection from Wayfarer's underside to the close charging island then onward to the foreground cargo island helps clearly establish vertical depth. Do not cover the central tower or front apron with cables. Avoid a symmetric stack, orbital helix, centered chandelier or four equally spaced corners.
Ships should fly at different levels: cargo traffic below the main ring, two passenger shuttles approaching the upper station apron, one service drone near the elevated power relay. Shadows, overlap at small edges only, visible undersides and perspective scale reinforce the depth. Leave most of the middle-left and lower-middle open as a three-dimensional arrival corridor. The image feels like a growing orbital dock district using the full volume of space, with one large station above an irregular constellation of service decks.
